references.text: Before the fall, Adam and Eve were naked without shame, a situation that changed dramatically after they ate from the tree of knowledge.
The serpent's promise that their eyes would be opened was fulfilled in 3:7—but not as they expected. Instead of divine insight, they gained awareness of their nakedness and shame.
God made garments of skin for Adam and Eve—his solution instead of their inadequate attempt with fig leaves, and a picture of God himself covering human sin.
Nakedness as an expression of shame and vulnerability, as Adam and Eve experienced it after the fall.
Nakedness as a symbol of spiritual poverty, with an invitation to receive white garments from Christ—a contrast to Adam and Eve's attempt to cover themselves.
The garment of salvation and the robe of righteousness as God's gift, in contrast to humanity's own attempts to cover their shame with fig leaves.
